newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares edge higher on institutional trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares edge higher on institutional trade.

text.p: Mutual funds continued to pick at Egyptian stocks on Thursday, firming overall share prices in quiet trading dominated by cement and milling firms.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index edged 2.44 points or 0.6 percent to 384.8 points in slow trading worth 46.64 million pounds ($13.73 million).
"The funds are the main players now and there's a lot of foreign money trickling in and they like what they see," said Tarek Lotfy, institutional broker at Intercapital.

"The flow will probably increase within the next couple of weeks. There's a lot of money sidelined, waiting for the big foreign money to come in and bid up prices. Then we'll see a lot more buying and selling rather than one-sided deals," he added.
Funds were also behind most of Wednesday's heavy trading and brokers said they were taking strong positions in the cement and milling sectors.

Amriyah Cement took over the top spot from rival firm Helwan Portland Cement in turnover, rising 0.5 pounds to 86.5 in trade worth 9.1 million pounds. Helwan came second best after topping turnover for the past two days with deals at 8.1 million pounds but shares ended unchanged at 79.

A flurry of activity also hit the milling sector, and particularly North Cairo Flour Mills and Upper Egypt Flour Mills. North Cairo rose one pound to 192 while Upper Egypt fell a slight 0.6 pounds 88.5.
Brokers said the funds liked the mills and cements because of their growth potential.
Other promising shares include realty firm Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, which rose three pounds to 495, and Egyptian Financial and Industrial which gained four pounds to 215.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 592.2 points from 585.54 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also increased to 266.98 from to 266.08.
Out of the 82 shares traded, 33 gained, 29 lost and 20 ended unchanged.
